what: Greedy decoding on this machine is not reproducible across processes. Measured 2026-08-24 on gfx1100, TP=2, as a by-product of verifying an unrelated kernel change.
why_it_surfaced: The sliding-window block-skip change was being verified by comparing generated token ids before and after. Sequences differed at depths where the change provably does nothing, including 512 tokens against a 2048 window, so the test itself was suspect rather than the change.
method: vLLM 0.23.1.dev, TP=2, greedy (temperature 0, ignore_eos), 64 generated tokens, synthetic repeating-token prompt, one warm-up generate of the same prompt before the measured one. Three independent processes per (model, kernel state, depth). No code differs between the three runs of a cell.

result.note: Symmetric between the two kernel states, so the change under test is not the cause.

reading: 10 of 36 cells produced more than one greedy output across three runs with no code change between them. It appears at any depth, including 512 tokens, and the first divergence is usually early, index 0 to 9 of 64, after which greedy decoding amplifies it. gemma-4-31B, which runs on the TRITON_ATTN backend, was deterministic in all four of its cells; the affected models are on ROCM_ATTN and its Triton kernel_paged_attention_2d. The kernel itself is not the source: 15 fixed-input cases run in two separate processes agreed bit for bit (torch.equal), so whatever varies is above the kernel, in the engine.
relation_to_upstream: vllm#50603, open since 2026-07-31, reports first-call non-determinism and long-sequence corruption from the same Triton paged-attention fallback on gfx1100, and names gqa_ratio=2 as what gates the CK custom kernel out. gemma-3-27b has gqa_ratio exactly 2. **One detail does not match: that report says a warm-up call fixes the non-determinism, and every measurement here already includes a warm-up generate of the same prompt at the same depth.** Whether this is the same defect seen from a different angle, or a second one, is not settled and nothing has been posted to that issue.
not_established: Not tested: the same within-process experiment on the unpatched kernel. The argument that the block-skip change is not implicated rests on Muse-Glimmer at 512 being below its own window, where the change is bit-identical by the boundary tests, and on the cross-process split being symmetric between the two kernel states, 5 and 5. A direct unpatched within-process run is about 17 minutes and has not been done. Also untested: TP=1, and whether the varying outputs are wrong or merely different. No claim is made that any output is incorrect.

within_process.why: vllm#50603 says a warm-up call fixes first-call non-determinism. Every cross-process measurement here already had a warm-up and still varied, so the question was whether a single process repeated is stable.
within_process.method: One engine, one prompt, a warm-up generate, then eight identical greedy generations back to back. Two independent processes per (model, depth) to check the pattern itself reproduces. Kernel patched, which matters only for the depths above each window; Muse-Glimmer at 512 is below its 2048 window, where the change is a proven no-op.
within_process.reading: The non-determinism is inside a single process, not an artefact of comparing processes, and a warm-up does not remove it. Muse-Glimmer at 512 tokens produced 7 distinct outputs in one process and 8 in the other, from eight identical greedy calls. It is model and depth dependent rather than uniform: gemma-3-27b at the same 512 depth was fully deterministic, 1 of 8 in both processes, while both models settled to 2 distinct outputs at 8192. The two processes agree on the pattern, so this is a property of the configuration rather than luck.
within_process.what_this_changes: The detail that did not match vllm#50603 is now measured rather than suspected: a warm-up call does not fix it here. Either that report's remedy does not generalise, or this is a second defect. Nothing has been posted to that issue.
